gate: MANDATORY GATE 8 — security/privacy production review of services/api + media handling

environment.stack: docker compose: postgres:5432 (pickle_dev), postgres-test:5433 (pickle_test), redis, MinIO (S3 API 9000), ElasticMQ
environment.api_under_test: live Fastify process, PICKLE_ENV=development, port 3901, real Postgres + real MinIO + presigned S3 URLs
not_available: real RevenueCat credentials (authorized-webhook success path unverifiable)
multi-instance/edge WAF deployment (shared rate-limit store unverifiable)

method.type: live black-box exploit testing against the running API + real object storage, plus code review and DB-backed regression tests
method.probe_scripts: 8 standalone probe suites (auth/privilege, authorization/IDOR + hostile input, media/signed URLs, privacy/consent/training, rate limiting + provider webhooks, secrets/log hygiene, erasure-vs-storage with the real media worker, configured billing webhook). Probes are local test harnesses, deliberately not committed; every count below was produced by executing them against the live stack.
attacker_models: authenticated user A attacking user B's resources by identifier
non-admin user attacking admin routes and self-granted role claims
holder of a valid presigned URL attempting scope escalation
direct anonymous access to the object store
method.counting_rule: one probe = one distinct attack attempt with a decisive expected-deny outcome; bursts are reported as request counts with the observed status-code histogram, never as probe counts

auth_bypass_and_privilege.covered: missing/empty/malformed Authorization, alg=none, HS256 with wrong secret, wrong issuer/audience, expired, not-yet-valid, subject swap, self-claimed pickle_role=admin, deleted user, suspended user, admin-route access as non-admin, admin route with no token
auth_bypass_and_privilege.note: dev HS256 verifier is env-gated (cannot construct outside development/test); staging/production fail closed without OIDC issuer/audience/JWKS

authorization_idor_and_hostile_input.covered: cross-user reads/mutations/deletes on media, sessions, shots, share cards, analyses, friends, consent, export; SQL-injection strings in path/query/body identifiers; UUID-shaped-but-foreign ids; NUL bytes and invalid UTF-8 in paths and bodies; oversized/deeply-nested/malformed JSON; header injection attempts; path-traversal segments

media_upload_and_signed_urls.covered: hostile filenames (traversal/NUL/absolute paths) → opaque server-generated key; declared-metadata validation (kind, size caps 500 MiB raw / 10 MiB thumbnail, content-type allowlist, sha256 shape); presigned PUT with tampered key → 403; presigned PUT with spoofed content-type → 403; honest PUT succeeds; oversized real object rejected at complete; stored-checksum mismatch rejected; content-type spoof rejected at complete; upload URL expiry ≤ 900s; playback URL expiry ≤ 300s; signature does not cover other keys; cross-user playback URL minting → 404; expired URL → 403; anonymous bucket list → 403; anonymous object read → 403; upload denied without cloud-sync consent
media_upload_and_signed_urls.note: the single API-only miss was byte residue of a *rejected* upload (purge is asynchronous); the first real media-worker sweep deleted it — measured, see erasure_vs_object_storage

privacy_deletion_export_consent_training.covered: export scoped to caller only; export/deletion of another user's account by id; consent grant/withdraw replay and forged subject; consent records immutable (UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE refused by DB policy); training eligibility requires latest granted model_training consent + all_captures scope; withdrawal removes eligibility; deleted user's dataset items deactivated

erasure_vs_object_storage.method: real media-worker runOnce() against real Postgres + real MinIO with the deleter now built from configuration
erasure_vs_object_storage.single_asset_deletion: derived artifacts present=2 → after one sweep=0; media_asset.object_key nulled, status=deleted
erasure_vs_object_storage.account_deletion: DELETE /v1/me → 200; one worker pass processed 3 deletion tasks; owned media bytes remaining=0; app_user rows remaining=0; deletion_task final state: media_purge=done, ml_dataset_review=done, final_hard_delete=done, idp_revoke=queued (blocked on IdP credentials, honestly reported by the worker, never marked done)

measured_after_fix./v1/health burst: 700 requests → {200: 700} (deliberately exempt: static in-memory response for load-balancer probes)

rate_limiting.caller_isolation: verified by regression test: throttling one caller does not throttle another
rate_limiting.limits: default 600 req/60s per caller, 60 req/60s per caller on expensive routes (media presign/complete/playback, export, consent export, friend requests, share cards, analyses, bootstrap, account deletion, billing sync)

billing_webhook_configured.covered: webhook without authorization → 401; near-miss authorization → 401; malformed body with valid authorization → typed 4xx (no 500); unmappable app_user_id → no 500; SQL-injection app_user_id → no 500 and app_user table intact; identical-event replay → identical typed outcome and zero entitlement mutation; client-claimed entitlement sync grants nothing
billing_webhook_configured.external_limit: with only a local fake RevenueCat key the authorized path terminates at upstream verification (502 billing.revenuecat_credentials_rejected); the real-credential success path is NOT verified here

secrets_and_log_hygiene.one_non_secret_match: .github/workflows/ci.yml:16 POSTGRES_PASSWORD: pickle_ci_password — an ephemeral CI service-container fixture, not a production credential (classified P2, no code change)
secrets_and_log_hygiene.build_output: `pnpm build` is typecheck-only (no bundling/emit), so there is no build artifact that could embed secrets

injection_and_ssrf_review.sql: all request-path queries use parameter arrays plus ownership predicates; no string-concatenated SQL found in services/api or services/media-worker; injection strings measured non-exploitable (see authorization_idor_and_hostile_input)
injection_and_ssrf_review.command: 0 child_process/shell uses in services/api and services/media-worker; the offline swing-lab tooling uses execFile/spawn with argument arrays and is not request-reachable
injection_and_ssrf_review.path_traversal: object keys are entirely server-generated (media/<owner uuid>/<24 random bytes>); client filenames never reach a key or filesystem path
injection_and_ssrf_review.ssrf: only outbound fetch on a request path is RevenueCat verification to a fixed https://api.revenuecat.com/v1/subscribers/<encoded id> with timeout; external instructional media URLs are validated to https + an approved YouTube/Vimeo host allowlist and are never server-fetched

regression_tests.root_gates: pnpm typecheck ✓, pnpm test ✓ (all 20 workspace projects, e.g. swing-lab 593 passed / 4 skipped), pnpm lint ✓, pnpm format:check ✓

P0.title: Share-card creation accepted another user's sessionId (cross-user IDOR)
P0.evidence: user A created a share card referencing user B's practice_session id and received 201
P0.impact: one user's session data could be embedded in another user's shareable artifact
P0.fix: ownership predicate on sessionId (404 when not owned) in services/api/src/modules/catalog/extraRoutes.ts
P0.regression_test: security-hardening.integration.test.ts — cross-user sessionId rejected, owner's own sessionId still accepted

P0.title: Media completion trusted client-declared integrity: no verification of stored checksum, size, or content type
P0.evidence: a presigned PUT of content whose bytes/type differed from the declaration completed to status ready
P0.impact: content-type spoofing and content substitution into the media pipeline (unsafe file upload)
P0.fix: presigned upload binds content-type, content-length and SHA-256 (x-amz-checksum-sha256) and the response returns the required headers; completion HEADs the stored object with checksum mode enabled and rejects size/type/checksum mismatch, marks the asset deleted and enqueues media.purge (services/api/src/modules/media/{routes,objectStore}.ts)
P0.regression_test: security-hardening.integration.test.ts — signed constraints asserted; checksum mismatch, missing checksum, and content-type spoof all rejected and purged; honest upload still completes

P0.title: Deployed media worker could never delete bytes: the entrypoint hardcoded objectStore = null
P0.evidence: services/media-worker/src/main.ts passed null, so media.purge returned handled=false and the media_purge deletion task re-queued as blocked; on the live stack a deleted asset's bytes stayed in the bucket indefinitely
P0.impact: right-to-erasure never executes in any deployment of this entrypoint — deleted users' and deleted assets' media bytes retained forever (the worker was honest about it, but erasure silently never completed)
P0.fix: buildObjectDeleter(env) (S3/MinIO delete + paginated prefix list) wired into the entrypoint (services/media-worker/src/objectStore.ts, src/main.ts)
P0.regression_test: media-worker/test/objectStore.test.ts (wiring: null when unconfigured, deleter with delete+list when configured) plus live measurement: single-asset derived artifacts 2 → 0 and account-deletion media bytes → 0 after real worker passes

P1.title: No rate limiting anywhere on the API
P1.evidence: pre-fix bursts all fully accepted: 300/300 health 200, 200/200 invalid-token 401, 120/120 media presigns 200, 40/40 exports 200 — unlimited credential-stuffing, handle enumeration, presign flooding and export amplification
P1.fix: per-caller route-aware limiter (services/api/src/plugins/rateLimitPlugin.ts): SHA-256 token fingerprint (never the raw token) or client IP, bounded key map (50k), 600 req/60s default, 60 req/60s on expensive routes, typed 429 api.rate_limited with Retry-After
P1.regression_test: security-hardening.integration.test.ts — expensive route throttles the abusing caller and leaves a second caller unaffected
P1.residual_risk: the limiter is per process; with N API instances the effective per-caller budget is N × budget. An edge/WAF or shared-store limit is still required before broad release — this is deployment-side and cannot be verified in this environment.

P1.title: Hostile identifiers produced logged 500s (NUL byte / invalid UTF-8 / malformed numerics), and Postgres error text carrying the offending value reached the logs
P1.evidence: pre-fix hostile run: 118 logged 500 responses and 98 Postgres invalid-input error lines
P1.fix: reject request paths containing NUL early, and map Postgres 22P02/22003/22021 plus Fastify parse/validation errors to typed 4xx envelopes (services/api/src/app.ts)
P1.post_fix_measurement: same hostile corpus (137 probes): 0 logged 500s, 0 Postgres error lines with the offending value
P1.regression_test: security-hardening.integration.test.ts — malformed identifiers, NUL paths and malformed JSON all typed 400/404

P2.title: CI service-container fixture password committed in .github/workflows/ci.yml
P2.assessment: ephemeral throwaway Postgres credential for the CI service container; not a production secret and not reachable from any deployed environment
P2.status: unresolved by choice (no change made; recorded for transparency)

P2.title: No orphan-object reconciliation by bucket listing
P2.assessment: purge and the sweep are driven from media_asset rows, so a bucket object whose row is already gone (only reachable by out-of-band writes, not by any API path) is never collected. Storage-cost/retention hygiene, no access-control impact.
P2.status: unresolved (out of gate scope, no evidence of an API path that creates such objects)

P2.title: /v1/health is exempt from rate limiting
P2.assessment: intentional: static in-memory response with no DB or storage access, needed for load-balancer probes. 700/700 accepted, measured.

unverified_external: RevenueCat authorized-webhook success path and subscriber verification (requires real provider credentials; locally the path terminates at a typed 502 and grants nothing)
Shared/edge rate limiting across multiple API instances (deployment-side; per-process limiter measured here)
deletion_task kind idp_revoke (requires identity-provider admin credentials; worker keeps it queued and never claims completion)
Production OIDC verification against a real issuer/JWKS (code fails closed without configuration; verified only by construction guards and unit tests)
rationale: Every exploitable finding discovered by live exploit testing against the real stack (3 × P0, 2 × P1) was fixed on this branch and re-measured post-fix: 85/85 auth-bypass probes blocked, 137/137 authorization/IDOR + hostile-input probes blocked with 0 logged 500s, 30/30 media/signed-URL probes blocked (the last one after the now-wired worker sweep), 21/21 privacy/consent/training probes blocked, 6/6 erasure-vs-real-storage probes blocked, 10/10 configured-webhook probes blocked, and 0 secrets/PII/tokens in 5237 scanned API log lines. No unresolved exploitable finding remains internally. The PASS is conditional on two deployment-side items that cannot be verified in this environment and must be closed before broad release: a shared edge/WAF rate limit across API instances (the in-process limiter is a partial mitigation), and real-credential verification of the RevenueCat webhook path. No device/iPhone/macOS measurement is claimed. Held-out cases wm-dink-01 and afn-vic-rally1 were not touched.
